# v0.8.4 - Verify Before You Believe

## What's Changed in v0.8.4

Two findings from `REVIEW.sonnet.md` that the v0.8.3 pass deferred, both of them cases where the code was trusted for something it had not checked: the lock believed a clock estimate about who owned it, and `gc` believed an upload returned `True`. Neither is a protocol change — the ticket gains one field, the pack verification adds no format — and both now fail closed.

The lock fix closes a race that was **reproduced against a stateful store**: with the old ordering, two clients both end up marked as holders of one repository, and the first of them keeps pushing while the second does too.

### Fixed

- **A granted lock can no longer be preempted by a later arrival's clock.** The ticket queue ordered on `order_ts`, a *client-side estimate* of server time — the local clock plus the offset implied by the `Date:` header, whose resolution is one second. That estimate is fine for deciding who *waits*: approximate shared time is all an expiry check needs. It was also deciding who *holds*, and that it cannot do, because two estimates half a second apart are indistinguishable from a genuinely earlier arrival. A newcomer whose estimate came out behind an active holder's therefore sorted ahead of it and acquired the lock while the holder was mid-push — with its own ticket intact and unexpired, so nothing a ticket read could detect. A winning client now publishes `"holding": true` on its ticket, and the queue sorts every granted ticket ahead of every ticket that has merely asked, whatever the timestamps say; `order_ts` is demoted to the tie-break among peers. The marker is written in a second pass, after the queue has agreed the client won, so `holding` always means "granted" and never "asked" — a marker written on the first upload would claim the lock before it was awarded. It takes effect once every client pushing to the repository is on v0.8.4+: a newer client will not preempt an older holder, but an older client ignores the marker and can still preempt a newer holder.
- **The ownership fence now looks at the queue, not only at our own ticket.** `verify_ownership()` was `return self.renew()`, which proves the *lease* — the ticket is gone or foreign once another client reaps it — and nothing else. It could not see the failure above, because in that failure our own ticket is still there, still ours, still unexpired: it reads back perfectly while the queue has already given the lock away. The fence now also scans the queue and fails when an active ticket sorts ahead of ours, reported as a third state, `another client was granted the lock while this ticket was still held`, kept distinct from a takeover because the two send an operator to different places. The scan is read-only — a verification step that reaped tickets would be doing acquisition's job — and rate-limited to one listing per second, so fencing once per deleted ref does not list the queue once per ref. The lease itself is still re-proven on every call, so a ticket that has been *reaped* is caught immediately rather than once per window.
- **`gc` no longer deletes the old packfiles on the strength of an unverified upload.** After `repack -a -d` the consolidated pack and index were uploaded and *all* superseded packs were then deleted, with only two checks between: that `upload_file` returned `True` and that the lease was still held. Nothing confirmed the new pack was actually there and intact — a truncated write, a quota error that a proxy answered `2xx`, or an `.idx` that never landed would all pass and the old packs would then be removed. For a tool whose product is "your repository's only copy", that is the step that deserves the most paranoia. The remote pack directory is now listed again and every new `.pack`/`.idx` must appear at the size it has locally; anything else refuses, names what could not be verified, and leaves every old packfile in place. Until the new ones are proven present, the old ones are still the only complete copy.
- **The delete loop fences every deletion, and losing the lease no longer reads as a no-op.** The result of `maybe_renew()` was discarded in the deletion loop, and since its `False` also means "the renewal interval has not elapsed" — which is what most of its calls return — a lease lost mid-loop looked exactly like an ordinary no-op and the loop kept deleting packfiles inside another client's push. Ownership is now re-validated before *each* removal. Losing it part-way through stops the cleanup and says so rather than failing the run: the consolidated packfiles are verified by that point, so the leftovers are only clutter.

### Documentation

- `USER_GUIDE` §12 said ticket ordering "prevent[ed] write-write collision races and client clock drift". It did not, for the reason above. The section now separates what the ordering guarantees from what the `Date:` header can support, states the mixed-version limit of the marker, and describes the fence as the two-part check it is, with the distinct messages each failure produces.
- `USER_GUIDE` §10 and `DESIGN.md` §7.2 now describe what actually gates the pack deletions, and §10 records that compaction's scratch space comes from the system temporary directory (`TMPDIR`, or `TEMP`/`TMP` on Windows) — worth knowing before compacting a large library on a small `tmpfs`, where the run fails late and after the lock is taken.
- `lock-status` prints a `Granted` line when the winning ticket carries no marker, which means either a pre-v0.8.4 client or an abandoned queue `--force` would clear. It is not an error on its own, but it does mean the marker-based protection is not in force for that lock.

### Tests & Tooling

- `tests/test_lock.py` gains `TestHoldingMarkerOutranksTheServerTimeEstimate`: the skew preemption itself, the marker surviving a renewal (renewal rewrites the whole ticket body, so a marker added to only some of the writers would be dropped on the first refresh — and the ticket would still look well-formed), the new `LEASE_PREEMPTED` state, the reaping of a crashed holder that the marker must not turn into a permanent lock, the scan rate limit, and the sort key putting a grant ahead of an earlier estimate. Verified to fail with the marker removed from the ordering.
- `tests/test_gc.py` gains `TestGcVerifiesTheUploadBeforeDeletingAnything`: a truncated pack, a pack absent from the listing, a listing failure during verification, and a lease lost mid-cleanup — each asserting that no packfile is deleted. The gc fixtures now model a remote whose pack listing grows with what it was sent; a listing frozen at its pre-upload state fails the new check, correctly, but for a reason that has nothing to do with the test.
- Suite: 630 → 640 tests across 123 targets, all green; docs guards 10/10; ruff clean.
